title: Japan Tops India FDI with $5.71 Billion in Q1 FY27
excerpt: India’s investment relationship with Japan has entered a potentially transformative phase. Japan has emerged as the country’s largest source of foreign direct investment during the April–June quarter of FY 2026-27, contributing an impressive $5.71 billion in equity inflows, according to government data. The figure is particularly significant because it exceeds the approximately $3.74 billion received from Japan during the entire previous financial year. Japanese investment accounted for nearly 29% of India's total equity FDI inflows of $19.81 billion during the first quarter, reflecting a remarkable concentration of Japanese capital in India's growth story. However, the importance of this development extends well beyond the investment figures. The emerging India–Japan economic partnership is increasingly being shaped by a strategic combination of Japanese capital, advanced manufacturing technology, Indian market potential and the growing importance of resilient global supply chains. For India's micro, small and medium enterprises, this changing investment landscape presents opportunities that could be far more consequential than the immediate rise in foreign capital. Understanding the $5.71 Billion Investment Surge Japan's emergence as India's leading investment partner in the first quarter reflects an important shift in the composition of Japanese investments. Traditionally, Japanese companies have built a strong industrial presence in India through automotive manufacturing, engineering, electronics, industrial machinery and infrastructure projects. Companies such as Suzuki, Toyota, Honda, Hitachi and Mitsubishi have become familiar names in India's industrial ecosystem. The latest investment wave, however, demonstrates that Japanese companies and financial institutions are beginning to look beyond conventional manufacturing investments. Banking, financial services, digital infrastructure, technology, renewable energy and corporate acquisitions are increasingly influencing Japan's investment strategy towards India. Nevertheless, the first-quarter numbers require careful interpretation. A substantial portion of the investment surge came from a single major financial-sector transaction, rather than a broad increase in new manufacturing factories. This distinction is important because the long-term economic impact of foreign investment depends not merely on how much capital enters the country, but also on where that capital is deployed and how effectively it stimulates domestic production, employment and business activity. MUFG–Shriram Finance Deal: Japanese Capital Moves Deeper Into India's Financial Ecosystem One of the most significant developments behind the investment surge was Japan's MUFG Bank completing its acquisition of a 20% stake in Shriram Finance Limited in April 2026. The transaction, valued at approximately ₹39,618 crore, represents the largest cross-border investment in India's financial services sector. MUFG subscribed to over 47.11 crore shares through a preferential allotment, providing substantial fresh equity capital to Shriram Finance. While this is an important financial transaction in its own right, the wider implications are particularly relevant for India's MSME financing landscape. Shriram Finance operates across several financing segments, including commercial vehicle loans, business loans, equipment financing and lending to smaller enterprises. For Indian MSMEs, access to affordable and timely institutional credit remains one of the most significant growth challenges. The strategic participation of a major Japanese banking institution in an established Indian NBFC could strengthen funding capacity, risk-management practices and the availability of longer-term capital. However, the actual benefit to small businesses will depend on whether the additional capital results in expanded lending, more competitive borrowing costs and improved credit accessibility. The transaction also demonstrates an important shift in Japanese investment thinking: India is increasingly being viewed not merely as a manufacturing destination, but also as a major financial services and consumer-market opportunity. India's ₹6–7 Lakh Crore Japanese Investment Ambition The investment surge comes against the backdrop of an ambitious bilateral economic roadmap. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to Japan in August 2025, both countries established a target of attracting 10 trillion Japanese yen in private investment into India over the following decade. The initiative aims to deepen industrial cooperation across manufacturing, infrastructure, technology, clean energy, digital innovation and strategic industries. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal reinforced this investment agenda during his August 2026 visit to Japan, holding discussions with senior government representatives, financial institutions and business leaders. The minister emphasised India's growing consumption market, industrial capabilities, expanding digital economy and improving investment environment. Yet the larger opportunity is not simply to attract Japanese money. India must aim to combine this capital with domestic industrial capabilities, innovation, job creation and the expansion of Indian-owned enterprises. That is where MSMEs become especially important. Why Japanese FDI Could Become a Game-Changer for Indian MSMEs India's MSME sector occupies a critical position in manufacturing, employment generation, exports and the supply chains of larger industries. Japanese investment can potentially strengthen this ecosystem through several interconnected channels. 1. Greater Opportunities for Indian Component Manufacturers Japanese automotive, electronics and engineering companies rely heavily on supplier ecosystems that operate according to demanding quality, efficiency and reliability standards. As these companies expand their manufacturing presence in India, domestic MSMEs could gain opportunities in precision engineering, industrial components, metal fabrication, electronics assemblies, plastics, packaging and logistics. For smaller Indian manufacturers, the opportunity is not limited to supplying Japanese companies operating within India. Those able to meet international manufacturing standards could eventually become part of global procurement networks. However, access to such supply chains will require investments in quality certifications, process automation, engineering capabilities and consistent delivery standards. 2. Technology Transfer and Industrial Productivity Japan's competitive advantage has historically included precision manufacturing, industrial automation, lean production and process excellence. Many Indian MSMEs continue to operate with limited automation, restricted research and development budgets and productivity constraints. Deeper Indo-Japanese industrial partnerships could encourage technology licensing, joint ventures, machinery upgrades and management knowledge-sharing. The potential impact can be substantial. For instance, an Indian precision-engineering MSME that gains access to better production technology may improve output quality, reduce waste and become eligible to supply larger domestic and international manufacturers. The objective should be to convert foreign investment into measurable improvements in Indian industrial productivity. 3. Strengthening MSME Credit and Financial Inclusion Japanese financial institutions are showing increasing interest in India's banking and non-banking financial sectors. If this engagement expands, Indian enterprises could potentially benefit from greater competition in business lending, better supply-chain financing structures and new products designed around commercial transactions. Supplier financing, machinery loans, working capital and export-related credit are particularly relevant. Nevertheless, Japanese capital entering Indian financial institutions does not automatically guarantee cheaper loans. Credit pricing, regulatory conditions and the financial health of borrowing enterprises will continue to determine financing outcomes. 4. Export-Oriented Manufacturing and Global Supply Chains Global manufacturers are reassessing supply-chain concentration amid geopolitical uncertainty, tariff-related risks and changing cost structures. India's attractiveness lies in the combination of a large domestic market, manufacturing workforce and expanding industrial infrastructure. Japanese companies exploring diversified production networks may create additional opportunities for Indian suppliers. Domestic MSMEs that can meet global compliance and delivery requirements could become valuable partners in this transition. Semiconductors, Batteries, EVs and AI: Where the Next Investment Wave May Emerge While financial services have driven a substantial portion of the recent investment surge, several technology-intensive industries could shape the next phase of economic cooperation. Semiconductors and electronics: India's semiconductor ambitions require substantial capital, specialised equipment, materials, testing facilities and global technology partnerships. Japanese companies possess capabilities in semiconductor equipment, specialty chemicals, electronic materials and precision manufacturing. Electric vehicles and advanced mobility: Japan's established strengths in automotive engineering and mobility systems could support opportunities in EV components, hybrid technologies, batteries, motors, power electronics and advanced automotive supply chains. Critical minerals and battery materials: As clean energy and next-generation mobility grow, resilient supply chains for critical minerals and battery materials are becoming strategically important. Artificial intelligence and industrial automation: Japanese industrial expertise combined with Indian software capabilities could encourage joint development of smart factories, industrial robotics, predictive maintenance technologies and intelligent production systems. Renewable energy and energy efficiency: Opportunities may emerge in industrial energy systems, power electronics, storage solutions and low-carbon manufacturing. For Indian MSMEs, these areas should not be viewed merely as industries attracting large multinational corporations. They also represent potential entry points into specialised component manufacturing, engineering services and industrial technology development. Japanese Industrial Townships: Turning Investment Intent Into Manufacturing Activity A defining element of India's efforts to attract Japanese investors is the development of dedicated industrial ecosystems. Japanese industrial townships are intended to simplify investment processes by offering infrastructure, business facilitation and support suited to Japanese companies. These industrial clusters can support investors through regulatory coordination, industrial utilities, logistical access and institutional engagement. The industrial township model is especially relevant because major manufacturing investments rarely operate in isolation. A large automotive or electronics factory may require hundreds of supporting businesses supplying components, tools, maintenance services, packaging, transportation and specialised engineering. This creates an opportunity for Indian MSMEs located around such industrial clusters. The challenge is to ensure that domestic enterprises are integrated into these supply chains rather than remaining outside the benefits of foreign-led industrial expansion. Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Other States Could Benefit Japanese investment also has important implications for India's state-level industrial development. Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh possess significant industrial ecosystems capable of attracting different categories of investment. Tamil Nadu's strengths in automotive manufacturing, electronics and industrial infrastructure make it an important destination for advanced manufacturing opportunities. Maharashtra's financial ecosystem, industrial base and technology capabilities offer opportunities across financial services, engineering, logistics and digital infrastructure. Gujarat's industrial clusters, ports, chemicals ecosystem and emerging advanced-manufacturing projects provide a foundation for strategic industrial partnerships. Similarly, Uttar Pradesh has an opportunity to position its electronics, automotive components, defence manufacturing, food processing and industrial corridors as potential destinations for Japanese collaboration. During bilateral investment engagements in August 2026, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal specifically highlighted opportunities for Japanese technology and expertise to complement Uttar Pradesh's workforce and expanding industrial environment. The next competitive advantage for Indian states will increasingly depend on their ability to create investment-ready industrial ecosystems rather than relying only on financial incentives. What India Must Do to Convert Japanese Investment Into Sustainable MSME Growth India's opportunity lies in turning investment announcements into sustained industrial development. A few priorities deserve particular attention. First, strengthen supplier-development programmes. Indian MSMEs should receive structured opportunities to understand the procurement requirements of Japanese companies and upgrade their manufacturing capabilities accordingly. Second, create dedicated India–Japan MSME business-connect platforms. Industry associations, state governments and Japanese trade-promotion institutions should facilitate targeted buyer-seller interactions and technology partnerships. Third, improve access to industrial finance. MSMEs require affordable equipment loans, working-capital facilities and export-oriented financial products to participate in larger supply chains. Fourth, strengthen technical skills. Precision manufacturing, robotics, industrial automation, electronics and quality-management capabilities should receive greater attention in vocational and professional training. Fifth, encourage joint ventures and technology partnerships. The objective should be to build Indian enterprises capable of moving up the value chain rather than remaining exclusively low-margin suppliers. Finally, measure the quality of FDI. Policymakers should evaluate employment generation, domestic sourcing, technology transfer, exports and MSME participation alongside headline investment figures. Challenges That Could Limit the Impact Despite the strong investment momentum, several challenges remain. Japanese manufacturers are known for demanding quality standards, strong operational discipline and long-term planning. Many smaller Indian enterprises may require considerable improvements in manufacturing consistency, productivity, financial transparency and technical capabilities before joining these supply chains. Land availability, infrastructure, complex compliance requirements, skilled manpower and policy predictability may also influence future investment decisions. Another concern is the concentration of investment. The $5.71 billion quarterly figure is impressive, but a single major financial-sector transaction contributed a substantial portion of the total. Therefore, it would be misleading to interpret the entire increase as immediate evidence of a widespread manufacturing investment boom. The more meaningful indicator will be whether Japanese companies continue to announce and execute fresh manufacturing investments, expand industrial capacity, establish new research centres and develop domestic supplier networks over the coming years. SMEStreet Exclusive Perspective: India Must Move From Attracting Capital to Building Industrial Capability Japan's emergence as the largest source of FDI during the opening quarter of FY27 sends an encouraging signal about international investor interest in India's economy. However, foreign direct investment should not be evaluated only through the lens of capital inflows. For India, the strategic question is whether such investment helps the country develop stronger domestic enterprises, globally competitive industrial clusters and technologically advanced manufacturing capabilities. Japanese capital can support industrial expansion. Japanese technology can improve productivity. Japanese manufacturing expertise can strengthen production quality and operational efficiency. India, meanwhile, offers market scale, entrepreneurial talent, digital capabilities and an expanding industrial ecosystem. The combination is promising. But the real economic multiplier will emerge only when India's MSMEs become active participants in this relationship. A small engineering business graduating into a global supplier, an Indian technology company entering a joint development arrangement, or a manufacturing MSME gaining access to export markets through Japanese collaboration would represent tangible examples of investment-led economic progress. The ₹6–7 lakh crore-equivalent Japanese investment ambition should therefore be viewed not only as a funding target, but as an opportunity to transform industrial capabilities. India's next milestone should not merely be attracting more Japanese investment. It should be ensuring that every major investment creates new opportunities for Indian manufacturing, technology, employment and MSME entrepreneurship. That is how the India–Japan economic partnership can evolve from a story of capital movement into a story of sustainable industrial transformation. About the Author Dr Faiz Askari is the Founder and Editor of SMEStreet and Founder and Director of Vertical Business Media Pvt. Ltd. With over a decade of engagement in India's MSME and entrepreneurial ecosystem, he writes on economic policy, industrial transformation, investment trends, business growth and international trade. His analysis focuses on connecting major economic developments with practical opportunities for Indian entrepreneurs and emerging enterprises.

title: K’taka govt launches ‘ELEVATE Minorities’, ‘NxT Startup’ schemes with grants up to Rs 1 crore
excerpt: Bengaluru, Oct 12 (IANS) The Karnataka government on Monday announced the launch of ELEVATE Minorities 2026 and ELEVATE NxT 2026-27, offering grant-in-aid of up to Rs 50 lakh for minority entrepreneurs and Rs 1 crore for DeepTech startups to promote inclusive entrepreneurship and innovation. The Department of Electronics, IT and Biotechnology said applications for both programmes will open on October 13 and close on November 13, 2026. Applications can be submitted through the department’s official website. Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Information Technology, Biotechnology and E-Governance, said the initiatives reflected the government’s commitment to building an inclusive, innovation-driven startup ecosystem. While ELEVATE Minorities aims to provide early-stage funding and ecosystem support to entrepreneurs from minority communities, ELEVATE NxT focuses on startups developing advanced technologies rooted in scientific discovery and engineering. Custom Ad: Multiplex Under ELEVATE Minorities 2026, eligible startups can receive a one-time grant of up to Rs 50 lakh for prototype development, market development and scaling up their businesses. Selected startups will also receive mentoring and incubation support through government-backed centres at subsidised rates. The programme is open to entrepreneurs belonging to minority communities recognised by the Karnataka State Minorities Commission and the Karnataka Minorities Development Corporation, including Muslims, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs and Parsis. The selection process will involve online applications, eligibility and document verification, in-person pitching, and a Grand Finale. Applicants will be assessed on innovation, socio-economic impact, business model, team capability and budget utilisation. Startups scoring at least 60 marks will qualify for the Grand Finale. ELEVATE NxT 2026–27, the second edition of the DeepTech grant programme, offers financial assistance of up to Rs 1 crore to eligible startups. Priority sectors include artificial intelligence, generative AI, quantum technologies, drones, autonomous systems, robotics, advanced materials, industrial automation and space technologies. The inaugural edition received 983 applications from across India and supported 33 DeepTech startups with Rs 30 crore in seed funding. Twelve of the supported startups were led by women entrepreneurs. The selection process for ELEVATE NxT will include application submission, eligibility screening, DeepTech qualification assessment, pitching and Grand Finale evaluation. Applicants will be assessed on scientific foundations, research and development, commercialisation strategy, socio-economic impact, founding team expertise and budget utilisation. Grant assistance under both programmes will be disbursed in two tranches, linked to completion of formalities and achievement of approved milestones. Selected startups will also receive mentorship, incubation, technology validation support and market linkages through the state's innovation ecosystem. --IANS mka/dan

title: As AI Reshapes Work and Wellbeing, Menthra Asks: What Is the Human Advantage?
excerpt: As artificial intelligence rapidly transforms the way people work, create, communicate and make decisions, Menthra brought together a diverse community of leaders and changemakers for ‘Human Advantage’, a gathering at Avasa Hotel, HITEC City, built around a fundamental question: “As AI becomes more capable, what becomes more valuable about being human?” Bringing together voices from business, technology, healthcare, psychology, education, entrepreneurship and the creative community, the event explored the human capabilities that will be critical to thriving alongside AI, including emotional wellbeing, resilience, connection, creativity and leadership. The event came at a significant moment for the global mental health conversation. This year’s World Mental Health Day theme, ‘Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change’, calls for people with lived experience to have a meaningful role in shaping mental health policies, services and decisions. Human Advantage built on this idea by creating a space where different experiences and perspectives could come together, not only to discuss technology, but to examine its impact on human connection, emotional wellbeing, resilience, creativity, leadership and the way we live and work. The day moved through three connected movements. The first rediscovered human possibility and what changes as machines grow more capable: what becomes more valuable in us, and how we move through change. The second looked at balance at work, at progress measured against humanity, and at mental wellbeing. The third turned forward, to who we become, what we choose to build, and ultimately what all of it is for. It closed where responsibility belongs, with human choice. Speaking at the event, Dinakara Nagalla, founder of Menthra, said: “AI will change the way we live and work, but our greatest advantage will always be our ability to be human. Human Advantage was about recognising that the future isn’t only about smarter technology. It’s about stronger, more resilient and more connected people.” The speakers were: Srikanth Bolla, Chairman, Bollant Industries Mihir Ahuja, Actor, Singer and Beatboxer Dr. Rajorshi Ganguli, President and Global HR Head, Alkem Laboratories Radhakrishna Bollineni, VP (AI), IBM Voleti Karthik, Founder, Flashoot Prerana Nayak, GM (Health, India), Microsoft AI Sathwik Maanthini, Founder, Communitie Garima Deveshwar-Bahl, Founder, Avasaram Leadership Deepti Varma, VP, PXT, Amazon Stores Sarita Sarkar, Founder, Sarkar’s Kitchen and Madikeri Craft Coffee Meraj Faheem, CEO (i/c), Telangana Innovation Cell, Government of Telangana Prof. Ashok Kumar Pandey, Professor and Dean (Academics), IIT Hyderabad Manisha Saboo, Chief Executive, Infosys Foundation Dr. Ch. Preeti Reddy, Vice Chairperson, Malla Reddy Vishwavidyapeeth Prashant Jain, Founder, shaant.ai Illusionist and mentalist Chirag Jethwaney gave a featured experience. The speakers’ perspectives added depth to the conversations around human potential, wellbeing, leadership and the evolving role of humanity in the age of AI. Menthra believes that the future of technology and human wellbeing cannot be viewed separately. As AI becomes increasingly embedded in everyday life, the ability to understand and support human emotional wellbeing will be central to helping individuals and organisations adapt, grow and thrive.

title: MP Cabinet pledges to build developed state by 2047, credits PM Modi’s leadership
excerpt: Bhopal, Oct 12 (IANS) The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet on Monday pledged to work towards building a developed state by 2047, aligning its development agenda with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of a developed India, while highlighting investments, infrastructure expansion, employment generation and welfare initiatives. At a special meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav at the Mantralaya, the Council of Ministers adopted a resolution marking 25 years of Modi’s public life, describing his tenure as an inspiration for governance and development. Yadav later briefed the media on the resolution, which also outlined the state government’s priorities and achievements under the BJP’s double-engine government. “By making Prime Minister Modi’s mantra our mission and leveraging our capabilities and dedication, we will build a developed Madhya Pradesh for a developed India,” Yadav said. Custom Ad: Multiplex The resolution highlighted major infrastructure and investment projects in Madhya Pradesh, including the Ken-Betwa, Parvati-Kalisindh-Chambal and Tapi basin projects aimed at expanding irrigation capacity. It also cited the development of metro rail projects worth around Rs 23,000 crore in Bhopal and Indore, improved air connectivity and the establishment of the PM MITRA textile park in Dhar. The state government said investment proposals worth more than Rs 30.77 lakh crore were received during the Global Investors Summit 2025, with projects worth around Rs 10 lakh crore under implementation. The state has introduced 25 industrial policies to facilitate investments, while a telecom manufacturing zone is planned in Gwalior. Yadav said PM Modi’s 25 years in public life, from serving as Gujarat Chief Minister to leading the country, reflected sustained efforts towards public welfare and national development. “Through tireless and ceaseless effort over his 25 years of public service, the Prime Minister has not only made resolutions but has also successfully realised them,” he said. The resolution also highlighted the state’s wildlife conservation efforts, noting that Madhya Pradesh’s cheetah population had reached 60, with habitats established at Kuno, Gandhi Sagar and Veerangana Rani Durgavati Tiger Reserves. On employment, the government said it aims to create more than two lakh government jobs. Plans for the coming year include 12 new medical colleges, 12 skill universities, industry-oriented training for one lakh youths and artificial intelligence and advanced computing laboratories in colleges. The cabinet cited women’s self-help groups, irrigation projects, renewable energy expansion and public transport initiatives among the state’s development priorities. It also noted that the Madhya Pradesh Assembly had passed the Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, by a voice vote. “The state government is committed to working shoulder-to-shoulder with the Prime Minister’s leadership to realise the goal of a developed Madhya Pradesh and a self-reliant India,” Yadav said. The resolution further referred to preparations for the 2028 Simhastha in Ujjain, with the government targeting completion of the related development works by Diwali 2027. --IANS pd/dan

title: MP Cabinet passes multi-pronged special resolution on PM Modi’s 25 years in public life
excerpt: Bhopal, Oct 12 (IANS) The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet on Monday unanimously passed a special resolution to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s public life. The Council of Ministers expressed gratitude and best wishes on “behalf of the state’s more than 8.5 crore people” for his journey from Chief Minister of Gujarat to the Prime Minister of India. The resolution wishes the Prime Minister a long life, good health and continued success. Addressing mediapersons here, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said the resolution was passed to affirm the state’s commitment to his mantra of “We Will Do It” and described the last 25 years as a chapter of service, good governance and nation-first spirit. Highlighting national achievements under the Prime Minister’s leadership, Chief Minister Yadav said the resolution notes that free food grains are being provided to over 80 crore citizens. Schemes such as Jan Dhan, Mudra, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, Ayushman Bharat, Swamitva, PM SVANidhi and Ujjwala have made Antyodaya meaningful. Custom Ad: Multiplex He pointed out that the resolution also recalls landmark reforms including demonetisation, GST, the Triple Talaq law, new criminal codes, the creation of NITI Aayog, PM Gati Shakti and Ease of Doing Business initiatives. On the digital front, the resolution points out that nearly 40 per cent of the world’s digital transactions now take place in India through UPI, CM Yadav said. Missions such as the Semiconductor Mission, National Quantum Mission and India AI Mission, along with more than two lakh start-ups, are shaping the future of technology and entrepreneurship. The National Education Policy 2020, women’s reservation through the Nari Shakti Vandan Act, abolition of Article 370, surgical strikes, Balakot airstrike, Operation Sindoor, Chandrayaan missions, the Ram Temple, and the rejuvenation of Kashi Vishwanath and Mahakal Lok are also mentioned in the resolution. Turning to Madhya Pradesh, the chief minister said that the resolution credits the double-engine government for major gains in irrigation through the Ken-Betwa, Parvati-Kalisindh-Chambal and Tapi projects, and for making the state Naxal-free. The resolution also notes the successful establishment of cheetah habitats, metro projects worth Rs 23,000 crore in Bhopal and Indore, the renaming of Bhopal’s railway station after Rani Kamalapati, and the state’s leadership in clean energy, with 30 per cent of its more than 30,000 MW capacity coming from renewable sources. The Chief Minister also highlighted the passage of the Uniform Civil Code Bill, empowerment of 65 lakh women through self-help groups, plans for over two lakh government jobs, and 20 per cent reservation for Agniveers in uniformed services. Investment proposals exceeding Rs 30.77 lakh crore under GIS-2025 further underscore the state’s growth trajectory under the Prime Minister’s guidance. There was a time when many countries around the world believed that India was developing and would remain so, but under your able leadership the tables have turned, and today the whole world unanimously acknowledges India’s rising stature under the “Modi hai to Mumkin hai” slogan, the Chief Minister said. The Prime Minister has recognised the young generation as both the creators and beneficiaries of a developed India, and the Madhya Pradesh government is laying a strong foundation for their future. More than two lakh new government jobs will be created in the state, a special examination of the Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission will be held once a year, 12 new medical colleges and 12 skill universities will be opened next year, one lakh youth will be linked with industry-oriented skills, and AI and Advanced Computing Labs will be established in colleges to equip them with future technologies, CM Yadav said. Through the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan-2026, your mantra of public welfare through public services has been transformed into a statewide mission, with citizens expressing their gratitude towards your sensitive and service-oriented leadership by lighting more than 3 crore 87 lakh lamps under the Ashirwad Ka Diya programme, including a new world record of over 33 lakh 27 thousand lamps lit in Ujjain, he said. --IANS sktr/dan

title: UK Trade Mission in India: Announces £1bn worth deal in AI, agriculture, education & manufacturing; Spurs job creation
excerpt: NEW DELHI: A major UK trade mission to India has announced more than Great British Pound(GBP) 1 billion in new commercial deals, including a GBP 50 million investment in Artificial Intelligence research. The deal also includes an expansion of aviation services by Menzies Aviation, as both countries seek to strengthen trade and investment ties following the implementation of the landmark free trade agreement. According to a release issued by the British High Commission, the announcement comes as a UK trade delegation comprising more than 100 businesses, the UK Business Secretary, the Secretaries of State for Scotland and Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, seven Mayors from northern England and a combined authority leader arrives in India to strengthen trade and investment ties between the two countries. During the visit, UK Business Secretary Reynolds also met Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in the national capital and co-chaired the UK-India Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO). “We co-chaired the 16th meeting of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) to advance our shared trade and economic priorities”, said Piyush Goyal. “Emphasised the importance of effectively using the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), addressing trade barriers and strengthening business-to-business engagement to translate the agreement’s opportunities into tangible outcomes. Reaffirmed our commitment to deepening India–UK economic cooperation through sustained engagement, stronger institutional mechanisms and enhanced collaboration, unlocking new opportunities for businesses in both countries”, Piyush Goyal further added. It is a pleasure to welcome UK Secretary of State for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, @JReynoldsMP and his delegation to India. We co-chaired the 16th meeting of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) to advance our shared trade and economic priorities.… pic.twitter.com/CrMWD6Ng82 — Piyush Goyal (@PiyushGoyal) October 12, 2026 Building momentum on the India-UK FTA; Advancing commercial partnerships The latest announcements build on the momentum generated by the UK-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA), with nearly GBP 12 billion worth of deals announced since the agreement was signed in July 2025. Among the key developments, Meta for Data Technologies (MFD) has announced a GBP 50 million investment to fund AI research in the UK, while UK-based aviation services company Menzies Aviation is seeking to generate more than GBP 600 million in revenue through an expanded presence in India. The trade mission aims to strengthen commercial partnerships across sectors, including advanced manufacturing, technology, aviation, education, agriculture and food and drink, while opening up new opportunities for businesses in both countries. UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said that the trade agreement had created opportunities for regional businesses, with northern England’s mayors playing a key role in developing partnerships to drive jobs, investment and economic growth. Both UK and India are already seeing the benefits of the landmark 🇬🇧🇮🇳 FTA, with nearly £12bn worth of trade and investment deals since the agreement was signed. UK Business Secretary @jreynoldsMP writes for the @EconomicTimes on how our countries are building on that momentum👇 pic.twitter.com/Vimig69mj9 — UK in India🇬🇧🇮🇳 (@UKinIndia) October 12, 2026 “From advanced manufacturing to education, we want to continue to deepen ties with one of the world’s fastest-growing economies to bring opportunity for businesses and consumers in all corners of both countries”, Reynolds said. The delegation also includes representatives from Scottish and British food and drink industries, including the Agriculture and Horticulture Development Board (AHDB), the British Meat Processors Association, Fever-Tree, Kendamil, the National Farmers’ Union, Salmon Scotland, the Scotch Whisky Association and Walker’s Shortbread. Scotland Secretary Douglas Alexander said the trade agreement would create opportunities for Scottish exporters, particularly producers of salmon and whisky, while encouraging inward investment and supporting employment in Scotland. “Scotland’s success in markets like India is supported by the strength, reach and influence that come from being part of the UK. Boosting export opportunities and encouraging inward investment in Scotland means real benefits back at home in economic growth and jobs,” he said. Also Read: “Army is the Rule, Army is the Law”: India slams Pakistan at UN; Exposes control of judiciary & press as mockery of law Environment, Food and Rural Affairs Secretary Angela Eagle said the government was working with British farmers and food and drink companies to translate the agreement’s commitments into tangible export opportunities. “We’re in India alongside food and drink exporters, helping them showcase the best of British produce, build new trading relationships, and unlock the export opportunities for communities across the UK”, she said. The UK Business Secretary will also co-chair the UK-India Science and Innovation Council with Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh. In Mumbai, the Business Secretary will meet Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to discuss closer regional economic cooperation and attend a trade marketplace showcasing British products and services. The visit comes three months after the UK-India trade agreement entered into force. The agreement is expected to increase bilateral trade by GBP 25.5 billion annually in the long term, according to the release. The mission underscores the two countries’ efforts to translate the trade pact into new business opportunities, export growth and employment across the UK and India. (With Inputs from ANI)
